title: The cave of Thawr
hookLine: three nights hidden in a cave, the searchers at its mouth, and the verse: Allah is with us (9:40)

lines: FEET AT THE MOUTH OF THE CAVE.
cards: Footsteps on rock, just overhead. Voices.
Men from Quraysh have tracked the fugitives up a mountain outside Mecca, and now they're standing at the mouth of a cave, close enough that the two men hiding inside can see their feet.
In the dark are the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, and Abu Bakr, his companion on the road out of Mecca. Neither of them moves. Neither of them breathes too loudly.

teach.h: IF HE LOOKS DOWN, HE'LL SEE US.
teach.b: In Sahih al-Bukhari, Abu Bakr remembers the moment himself. He whispers: if one of them looks down at his feet, he'll see us.

teach.h: TWO, WHEN GOD IS THEIR THIRD.
teach.b: And the Prophet answers: what do you think, Abu Bakr, of two when God is their third? One frightened sentence, one quiet question back. The Qur'an remembers the same night.

teach.h: GRIEVE NOT. LO! ALLAH IS WITH US.
teach.b: In Pickthall's translation, it speaks of when the two were in the cave, and he said to his companion: "Grieve not. Lo! Allah is with us." And God, the verse goes on, sent down His peace upon him.
Neither text has an escape plan, or a promise that the searchers will leave. Just: we are not two. The searchers do leave.
And Bukhari's longer account, from Aisha, shows how the hiding worked. They stayed in the cave three nights.

Abu Bakr's son Abdullah, a sharp young man, spent the nights with them and slipped back into Mecca before dawn, so that by day he was in the city like anyone else, listening for every plot against them, and brought the news back after dark.

teach.h: NEWS BY NIGHT, MILK, AND SHEEP.
teach.b: A freed servant of Abu Bakr's, Amir ibn Fuhayra, grazed sheep nearby, brought them milk in the evening, and moved on again before dawn. So faith in the story isn't the opposite of planning. The planning is careful.
It's the fear that gets answered, not with a plan, but with a question: two, and God the third.

how: Muslims recite 9:40 and retell the cave of Thawr when they remember the hijra, and Abu Bakr is remembered as the companion in the cave.

games.q: you're Abu Bakr. you can see the searchers' feet at the mouth of the cave. you whisper your fear. what does the Prophet say?
o: run for the back of the cave.
two, when God is their third.
games.why: he answered with a question: what do you think of two when God is their third? the Qur'an: grieve not, Allah is with us.

practice: Close your eyes, or cover them with your hands, and let the dark be what it is; notice your breath, and whatever worry is nearest, the way footsteps were nearest for Abu Bakr.

Without arguing with the fear, notice that you are not the only one in the dark: whoever you love, whoever is with you, and, if you believe, God. If you pray, you can say the line from the verse: Allah is with us.

wordCard.voice: Thawr. The mountain where the Prophet and Abu Bakr hid three nights, the searchers at the cave's mouth, and the Qur'an remembers: grieve not, Allah is with us. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: Thawr, the mountain where the cave is.

carryVoice: Your line: two, and Allah the third. Even in the dark, not alone. Day seven hundred sixty-six, done.
